reading.body:
Andreessen Horowitz is recorded as a for-profit venture investor with no products, no AI products, and no MCP servers attributed to it.

The record covers the firm's identity and location, not its portfolio. Founded in 2009 and headquartered in Menlo Park, California, it is classified as an investor, which means its relevance to AI compute runs through the companies it funds rather than anything it builds. None of those holdings appear here.

The 281 California law exposure entries are the only quantitative signal, and they are a count of legal exposure in one state, not a measure of investment activity. No individual cases are listed, so the figure cannot be broken down or attributed to specific matters.

What this does not tell a reader is where the firm's capital sits relative to data centers, power procurement, or chip supply. The data supports a statement about what the firm is and where it is registered. It does not support any claim about what it funds, and the absence of listed products should not be read as an absence of AI exposure.

profile_text.body:
Andreessen Horowitz, also known as a16z, describes itself as a venture capital firm in Silicon Valley, California, investing in bold founders, innovators, and entrepreneurs building the future through technology. Its website uses the tagline "Software Is Eating the World."

No specific products are listed for the firm, including no AI products or MCP servers. The firm is categorized as a for-profit investor, founded in 2009 and headquartered in Menlo Park, California, United States.

The firm is associated with 281 law exposure entries in California. No individual cases are listed.
